Core NATS is at-most-once and the owner enqueues before it replies: a reply lost twice (original and the one retry) gives a 503 although the message may be queued on the owner and, the persist step being skipped, is never recorded; the client may resend it and the run could read it twice. WS04-S6 (client_message_id, persist-then-enqueue) is what closes this; do not flip the switch for production before it.

A message over the bus is bounded at 8 KiB while the local bound is 2000 characters; a 2000-character message of 4-byte characters can exceed it and is answered as TooLong (413) with the character count even though it is within the character limit. Rare and safe, but the wording is slightly off.

The 'reply lost after the owner queued it' case is only simulated by sending the same op_id twice; the loopback hub cannot drop just the reply. A hub switch that delivers but swallows the reply would test the retry path in queue_input end to end.

results.notes: Built to the plan row with the bus switch off by default and unchanged behaviour with it off. 1) queued_input.rs: EnqueueOutcome is serde-capable (the retrieval scope goes over the wire as a string through a local module, because normalize.rs is not mine) and has a new ThreadMismatch arm. enqueue_checked merges thread_for and enqueue_for, so enqueue_for is gone. The mismatch check runs for the owning caller only; a stranger gets NoActiveStream. Bounded seen_ops (16, with the pending count answered) make a repeated op_id return the first answer and queue nothing. finish returns the number of undelivered messages. bus_message(claims, ...) is the only place text goes into a RunControlMsg and refuses ZDR and waived tokens again. 2) run_control.rs: the owner handler now answers Cancel, Queue and Probe. attach takes the QueuedInputRegistry. RunControl::queue_input is local-first, then the bus, with one retry on Timeout using the same op_id. ProducerLiveness is the local registry first, then a probe cached for 2 s. 3) http_routes.rs invoke_queue_input: gate, then bus_message, then queue_input. 409 for ThreadMismatch, the existing 404 with resend_as_new_turn for NoOwner or NoActiveStream, and 503 {queued:false, retryable:true, error:run_control_unavailable} with nothing persisted. Persist still follows enqueue (D3). The handler mints a server-side op_id per request. 4) sse.rs: one call-in change to attach; finish_stream_registrations counts queued_input_undelivered_total (via metrics::counter! directly, since gateway_metrics.rs is not owned) and logs a warn with the count only; invoke_resume_sse uses ProducerLiveness and the resume tail's timers moved from std::time::Instant to tokio::time::Instant so the 120 s window can be tested on a paused clock (behaviour is identical on a normal clock). 5) Tests: queue on B delivered via A's drain; Full(3), TooLong, Empty; foreign user, nobody-owns and non-token ids are the same 404; thread mismatch 409 from both replicas; duplicate op_id is one item across the bus; mute gives 503 and queues nothing; bus off gives the old 404; ZDR and waived callers put nothing on the bus (muted bus, owner queue stays empty); the probe keeps the resume tail past 130 s of virtual time and the tail closes after the owner finishes. Deviations: I did NOT edit zdr-posture-matrix.json or its .sha256 (see deviations).

shared-edit docs/compliance/evidence/honest-limits.md (CRLF), part a: insert after the L35 bullet (the last bullet of section 7, before '## 8. What Verevon does not have'):
- **L37. Audit rows are chained only where the chain is switched on, and the chain does not prove integrity against a database owner acting alone.** The chain is off unless `AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED` is set to `1`. Where it is on, the signing key sits outside the database, but the rows, their hashes and the attestations sit inside it. A database owner can rewrite rows and delete the attestations that cover them, and the rewritten chain then recomputes cleanly and is not reported as broken. Detection needs a signed head or checkpoint that covers the rewritten rows and is held outside the database, such as a SIEM copy or a customer export taken earlier.
- **L38. Completeness is not proven.** The chain covers the audit rows that were stored. An event that was never published, or that the consumer dead-lettered, is not in the chain, and the chain does not show that it is missing.
- **L39. Audit rows written before a chain was switched on are outside the chain, and they are never rewritten.** A verification report counts them and says that the chained part is verified, not the whole log.
- **L40. A SIEM copy is a witness only for the rows it has received, and only where a customer has configured a destination.** The exporter is off unless `AUDIT_SIEM_EXPORT_ENABLED` is set to `1`. A destination that is disabled, failing or not configured proves nothing about the rows it did not receive.

The details guard only counts oversize and denied keys (chain.go:30-38 and 332-335) and never rejects. The SIEM export sends details to customer endpoints, so content a producer puts in details reaches the customer's SIEM and is kept for the retention window. Decide enforce or observe before AUDIT_SIEM_EXPORT_ENABLED is switched on in any environment.

The enterprise entitlement that DEC-35 proposes for SIEM export (feature.siem_export; ruling Q-7a1-15) is not built. The operator switch ORG_SIEM_DESTINATIONS_ENABLED is the only gate on destinations, and the commercial ruling is open.

results.notes: Proto: InferRequest.prompt_tiers = 18, new message PromptTierPlan {stable_messages=1, context_messages=2}; additive only; no buf run (baseline.binpb is empty), the tag-diff is one new field at 18 and one new message. inference-core maps it to mp_contracts PromptTierPlan (default = none). Anthropic: INFERENCE_ANTHROPIC_TIERED_SYSTEM (strict parser, only "true", default off). When on, not ZDR, and the plan describes the request (counts within the message list, every counted message a system message), system becomes ordered blocks: Stable, Context, per-turn remainder (Volatile, never marked); apply_prompt_caching marks Stable and Context when the cumulative prefix clears the model minimum, so at most tools + 2 + last message = 4 breakpoints. ZDR gate is still the first statement of apply_prompt_caching, and a ZDR request never takes the tiered form (one plain system string). A plan that does not describe the request is ignored and the request is sent as today. With the switch off or no plan the body is byte-identical (tested). execution-core: the Do loop sends a plan read back from the round's messages (preamble = Stable 1; authored instructions = Context 1 only when messages[1] is that exact system text), None when the first message is not system. Counts only, no content logged. model-gateway tool_loop.rs: the InferRequest literal gets prompt_tiers: None.
